/**
 * Andah -- Timeless chrome.
 *
 * Loaded only for the Timeless skin. It adds the pieces of furniture the skin
 * does not emit, and which [[MediaWiki:Timeless.css]] therefore cannot style
 * into existence:
 *
 *   1. a header hamburger that collapses the site menu,
 *   2. the article table of contents, lifted into the left rail,
 *   3. an Appearance panel (text size / width / colour) at the foot of it,
 *   4. skip links, because the rails come last in the DOM,
 *
 * plus one rearrangement: Wiki tools moves from the left rail to the right.
 *
 * Nothing here paints. Every visual decision lives in Timeless.css; this file
 * only creates elements and writes preference classes onto <html>. If it fails
 * to run, the skin falls back to Timeless's own inline table of contents and
 * the extension's Dark mode link, which is why the CSS hides both of those on
 * classes this script sets rather than unconditionally.
 */
( function () {
	'use strict';

	/**
	 * Preferences.
	 *
	 * `feature` is both the storage key and the <html> class prefix, so
	 * andah-text/large becomes html.andah-text-clientpref-large. The suffix
	 * follows core's naming convention for readability; the values themselves
	 * are kept in localStorage, for the reasons set out below.
	 *
	 * Colour is the odd one out. It is stored as a preference of its own
	 * because it has a third state, Automatic, that core has no class for; what
	 * it actually drives is skin-theme, which the DarkMode extension watches.
	 * See applyTheme().
	 */
	var PREFS = [ {
		feature: 'andah-text',
		label: 'Text',
		def: 'standard',
		options: [
			[ 'small', 'Small' ],
			[ 'standard', 'Standard' ],
			[ 'large', 'Large' ]
		]
	}, {
		feature: 'andah-width',
		label: 'Width',
		def: 'standard',
		options: [
			[ 'standard', 'Standard' ],
			[ 'wide', 'Wide' ]
		]
	}, {
		feature: 'andah-theme',
		label: 'Colour',
		// Light, not Automatic: the wiki has always rendered light, and night
		// mode here is a whole-page inversion filter, so defaulting to the
		// reader's system setting would flip the look of the site under
		// everyone running a dark desktop without their ever asking for it.
		def: 'day',
		options: [
			[ 'os', 'Automatic' ],
			[ 'day', 'Light' ],
			[ 'night', 'Dark' ]
		]
	} ];

	// Not in the Appearance panel -- the hamburger is its own control -- but
	// stored the same way so the rail stays collapsed across page loads.
	var NAV_PREF = {
		feature: 'andah-nav',
		def: 'shown',
		options: [ [ 'shown' ], [ 'hidden' ] ]
	};

	/* --- preferences -------------------------------------------------------
	 * Stored in localStorage, as one object, and NOT in mw.user.clientPrefs.
	 * That API looks like the right home for these and is not, for two
	 * independent reasons:
	 *
	 *   1. clientPrefs.set() throws outright for a logged-in reader --
	 *      "clientPrefs are for unregistered users only". Since the throw
	 *      happened while saving, before the theme was applied, choosing Dark
	 *      did nothing at all for anyone with an account.
	 *
	 *   2. clientPrefs.get() reads the class list on <html>, not the cookie,
	 *      and MediaWiki only emits those classes server-side for features it
	 *      knows about. It has never heard of andah-text, so every page load
	 *      read back "unset" and fell to the default. The settings looked like
	 *      they persisted, because the cookie really was being written; nothing
	 *      ever read it again.
	 *
	 * localStorage has neither problem. The cost is a brief flash of the
	 * default before this runs, which is unavoidable without the skin
	 * rendering the classes itself.
	 */

	var STORE_KEY = 'andah-appearance';

	function readStore() {
		try {
			return JSON.parse( mw.storage.get( STORE_KEY ) || '{}' ) || {};
		} catch ( e ) {
			return {};
		}
	}

	function writeStore( feature, value ) {
		try {
			var all = readStore();
			all[ feature ] = value;
			mw.storage.set( STORE_KEY, JSON.stringify( all ) );
		} catch ( e ) {
			// Private browsing, a full quota, storage disabled. The setting
			// still applies to this page view; it just will not be remembered.
		}
	}

	function readPref( pref ) {
		var stored = readStore()[ pref.feature ],
			known = pref.options.some( function ( option ) {
				return option[ 0 ] === stored;
			} );
		return known ? stored : pref.def;
	}

	function applyClass( feature, value ) {
		var root = document.documentElement,
			prefix = feature + '-clientpref-';
		Array.prototype.slice.call( root.classList ).forEach( function ( name ) {
			if ( name.indexOf( prefix ) === 0 ) {
				root.classList.remove( name );
			}
		} );
		root.classList.add( prefix + value );
	}

	/**
	 * Apply first, remember second, and never let the remembering break the
	 * applying. Only called on an actual choice, so a reader who never opens
	 * the panel leaves no storage behind.
	 */
	function savePref( feature, value ) {
		applyClass( feature, value );
		writeStore( feature, value );
	}

	function prefersDark() {
		return !!( window.matchMedia &&
			window.matchMedia( '( prefers-color-scheme: dark )' ).matches );
	}

	/**
	 * Colour is delegated to the DarkMode extension rather than reimplemented:
	 * the extension owns the invert filter that the night palette in
	 * Timeless.css is authored against, and it keys that filter on core's
	 * skin-theme-clientpref-night class. So all this has to do is resolve
	 * Automatic against the system and set skin-theme accordingly. The
	 * extension has no Automatic of its own, which is the whole reason the
	 * reader's choice is stored separately as andah-theme.
	 */
	function applyTheme( mode ) {
		var night = mode === 'night' || ( mode === 'os' && prefersDark() );
		// The class only, never stored: what gets remembered is the reader's
		// andah-theme choice, which has three states. skin-theme is the
		// two-state class derived from it that the DarkMode extension watches,
		// and it is recomputed from andah-theme on every load.
		applyClass( 'skin-theme', night ? 'night' : 'day' );
	}

	/* --- building blocks ---------------------------------------------------
	 * A rail box, in Timeless's own shape:
	 *
	 *   div.sidebar-chunk > h2 > span            drawer toggle; the skin hides
	 *                                            this on desktop
	 *                     > div.sidebar-inner
	 *                       > div.mw-portlet
	 *                         > h3               the visible box title
	 *                         > div.mw-portlet-body
	 *
	 * Reproducing it exactly, rather than inventing something lighter, is what
	 * lets the two new boxes pick up the skin's own rail styling and its
	 * narrow-screen drawer behaviour for free. Content goes in .mw-portlet-body.
	 */

	function chunk( id, title ) {
		var box = document.createElement( 'div' ),
			h2 = document.createElement( 'h2' ),
			h2span = document.createElement( 'span' ),
			inner = document.createElement( 'div' ),
			portlet = document.createElement( 'div' ),
			h3 = document.createElement( 'h3' ),
			body = document.createElement( 'div' );

		box.id = id;
		box.className = 'sidebar-chunk';
		h2span.textContent = title;
		h2.appendChild( h2span );

		inner.className = 'sidebar-inner';
		portlet.className = 'mw-portlet';
		portlet.setAttribute( 'role', 'navigation' );
		h3.textContent = title;
		body.className = 'mw-portlet-body';

		portlet.appendChild( h3 );
		portlet.appendChild( body );
		inner.appendChild( portlet );
		box.appendChild( h2 );
		box.appendChild( inner );

		return box;
	}

	/**
	 * A hide/show control in a box's own heading, in the manner of Vector's.
	 * The state is remembered per box under its own key, so a reader who never
	 * wants the table of contents open does not have to close it on every
	 * article. The heading itself is left as a heading rather than being turned
	 * into a button: screen readers use those to navigate, and swallowing one
	 * to save a few pixels is a poor trade.
	 */
	function addCollapse( box, feature ) {
		var portlet = box.querySelector( '.mw-portlet' ),
			heading = box.querySelector( '.mw-portlet > h3' ),
			body = box.querySelector( '.mw-portlet-body' ),
			button = document.createElement( 'button' ),
			hidden = readStore()[ feature ] === 'hidden',
			// Read before the button goes in, or it ends up in its own label.
			label = heading.textContent.trim();

		button.type = 'button';
		button.className = 'andah-collapse';
		button.setAttribute( 'aria-controls', box.id + '-body' );
		body.id = box.id + '-body';

		function render() {
			button.textContent = hidden ? 'show' : 'hide';
			button.setAttribute( 'aria-expanded', hidden ? 'false' : 'true' );
			button.setAttribute( 'aria-label', ( hidden ? 'Show ' : 'Hide ' ) + label );
			body.hidden = hidden;
			portlet.classList.toggle( 'andah-collapsed', hidden );
		}

		button.addEventListener( 'click', function () {
			hidden = !hidden;
			writeStore( feature, hidden ? 'hidden' : 'shown' );
			render();
		} );

		heading.appendChild( button );
		render();
	}

	/* --- 1. hamburger ------------------------------------------------------ */

	function buildNavToggle() {
		var header = document.getElementById( 'mw-header' );
		if ( !header ) {
			return;
		}
		var button = document.createElement( 'button' ),
			bars = document.createElement( 'span' ),
			state = readPref( NAV_PREF );

		button.id = 'andah-nav-toggle';
		button.type = 'button';
		button.setAttribute( 'aria-controls', 'mw-site-navigation' );
		button.appendChild( bars );

		function render() {
			var hidden = state === 'hidden';
			button.setAttribute( 'aria-expanded', hidden ? 'false' : 'true' );
			button.title = hidden ? 'Show navigation' : 'Hide navigation';
			button.setAttribute( 'aria-label', button.title );
		}

		button.addEventListener( 'click', function () {
			state = state === 'hidden' ? 'shown' : 'hidden';
			savePref( NAV_PREF.feature, state );
			render();
		} );

		applyClass( NAV_PREF.feature, state );
		render();
		header.insertBefore( button, header.firstChild );
	}

	/* --- 1b. Wiki tools -----------------------------------------------------
	 * Timeless puts Wiki tools (Cite this page, Get shortened URL, ...) in the
	 * left rail, under site navigation. They are per-page tools, so they belong
	 * beside the rest of them on the right, and moving them leaves the left
	 * rail as navigation plus contents and nothing else.
	 */

	function moveWikiTools() {
		var tools = document.getElementById( 'site-tools' ),
			rail = document.getElementById( 'mw-related-navigation' );
		if ( tools && rail ) {
			rail.appendChild( tools );
		}
	}

	/* --- 2. table of contents ---------------------------------------------- */

	/**
	 * Rebuilds Timeless's inline TOC as a rail box rather than moving the
	 * original node, which carries a toggle checkbox and section numbering that
	 * only make sense inline. Sub-levels start collapsed; the top level never
	 * collapses.
	 */
	function buildToc() {
		var source = document.querySelector(
			'#mw-content-text #toc > ul, #mw-content-text .toc > ul'
		);
		if ( !source || !source.children.length ) {
			return;
		}

		var box = chunk( 'andah-toc', 'Contents' ),
			body = box.querySelector( '.mw-portlet-body' );

		function convert( sourceList, depth ) {
			var list = document.createElement( 'ul' );
			if ( depth === 0 ) {
				list.className = 'andah-toc-list';
			}
			Array.prototype.forEach.call( sourceList.children, function ( sourceItem ) {
				var sourceLink = sourceItem.querySelector( ':scope > a' ),
					sourceChildren = sourceItem.querySelector( ':scope > ul' );
				if ( !sourceLink ) {
					return;
				}
				var item = document.createElement( 'li' ),
					row = document.createElement( 'div' ),
					link = document.createElement( 'a' ),
					text = sourceLink.querySelector( '.toctext' );

				row.className = 'andah-toc-row';
				link.href = sourceLink.getAttribute( 'href' );
				link.textContent = ( text ? text.textContent : sourceLink.textContent ).trim();

				if ( sourceChildren ) {
					var toggle = document.createElement( 'button' ),
						children = convert( sourceChildren, depth + 1 );
					toggle.type = 'button';
					toggle.className = 'andah-toc-toggle';
					toggle.setAttribute( 'aria-expanded', 'false' );
					toggle.setAttribute( 'aria-label', 'Toggle ' + link.textContent + ' subsection' );
					children.hidden = true;
					toggle.addEventListener( 'click', function () {
						var open = toggle.getAttribute( 'aria-expanded' ) === 'true';
						toggle.setAttribute( 'aria-expanded', open ? 'false' : 'true' );
						children.hidden = open;
					} );
					row.appendChild( toggle );
					row.appendChild( link );
					item.appendChild( row );
					item.appendChild( children );
				} else {
					row.classList.add( 'andah-toc-leaf' );
					row.appendChild( link );
					item.appendChild( row );
				}
				list.appendChild( item );
			} );
			return list;
		}

		body.appendChild( convert( source, 0 ) );

		var rail = document.getElementById( 'mw-site-navigation' ),
			after = document.getElementById( 'site-navigation' );
		if ( !rail ) {
			return;
		}
		rail.insertBefore( box, after ? after.nextSibling : rail.firstChild );
		document.body.classList.add( 'andah-has-sidebar-toc' );

		addCollapse( box, 'andah-toc-state' );
		trackCurrentSection( box );
	}

	/**
	 * Marks the section the reader is in. A scroll listener rather than an
	 * IntersectionObserver: headings are points, not regions, so what is wanted
	 * is "the last heading above the fold", which an observer reports awkwardly.
	 */
	function trackCurrentSection( box ) {
		var rows = Array.prototype.map.call(
			box.querySelectorAll( '.andah-toc-row > a' ),
			function ( link ) {
				var id = decodeURIComponent( link.hash.slice( 1 ) );
				return { row: link.parentNode, heading: id && document.getElementById( id ) };
			}
		).filter( function ( entry ) {
			return entry.heading;
		} );
		if ( !rows.length ) {
			return;
		}

		var current = null,
			queued = false;

		function update() {
			queued = false;
			var best = null;
			rows.forEach( function ( entry ) {
				if ( entry.heading.getBoundingClientRect().top <= 80 ) {
					best = entry;
				}
			} );
			if ( best === current ) {
				return;
			}
			if ( current ) {
				current.row.classList.remove( 'andah-toc-current' );
			}
			if ( best ) {
				best.row.classList.add( 'andah-toc-current' );
				// Open every collapsed ancestor, or the mark is invisible.
				var node = best.row.parentNode;
				while ( node && node !== box ) {
					if ( node.nodeName === 'UL' && node.hidden ) {
						node.hidden = false;
						var toggle = node.previousSibling &&
							node.previousSibling.querySelector( '.andah-toc-toggle' );
						if ( toggle ) {
							toggle.setAttribute( 'aria-expanded', 'true' );
						}
					}
					node = node.parentNode;
				}
			}
			current = best;
		}

		window.addEventListener( 'scroll', function () {
			if ( !queued ) {
				queued = true;
				window.requestAnimationFrame( update );
			}
		}, { passive: true } );
		update();
	}

	/* --- 3. Appearance panel ----------------------------------------------- */

	function buildAppearance( values ) {
		var rail = document.getElementById( 'mw-related-navigation' );
		if ( !rail ) {
			return;
		}
		var box = chunk( 'andah-appearance', 'Appearance' ),
			body = box.querySelector( '.mw-portlet-body' );

		PREFS.forEach( function ( pref ) {
			var group = document.createElement( 'fieldset' ),
				legend = document.createElement( 'legend' );
			group.className = 'andah-pref-group';
			legend.textContent = pref.label;
			group.appendChild( legend );

			pref.options.forEach( function ( option ) {
				var label = document.createElement( 'label' ),
					input = document.createElement( 'input' ),
					text = document.createElement( 'span' );
				label.className = 'andah-pref-option';
				input.type = 'radio';
				input.name = pref.feature;
				input.value = option[ 0 ];
				input.checked = values[ pref.feature ] === option[ 0 ];
				text.textContent = option[ 1 ];
				input.addEventListener( 'change', function () {
					if ( !input.checked ) {
						return;
					}
					values[ pref.feature ] = option[ 0 ];
					savePref( pref.feature, option[ 0 ] );
					if ( pref.feature === 'andah-theme' ) {
						applyTheme( option[ 0 ] );
					}
				} );
				label.appendChild( input );
				label.appendChild( text );
				group.appendChild( label );
			} );

			body.appendChild( group );
		} );

		// LAST in the right rail, under Page tools and Wiki tools.
		//
		// It was first, which put a pinned box above two that scroll: the tools
		// slid up underneath it and vanished behind its own background, which
		// looks like a rendering fault rather than a design. Underneath them,
		// the tools scroll away cleanly off the top and this box pins once it
		// gets there, with nothing left to pass behind it.
		rail.appendChild( box );

		// Lets the CSS retire the DarkMode extension's own menu link, now that
		// this panel owns colour. Set here so the link survives if the panel
		// never gets built.
		addCollapse( box, 'andah-appearance-state' );
		document.body.classList.add( 'andah-has-appearance' );

		// Automatic has to keep tracking the system after the page has loaded.
		if ( window.matchMedia ) {
			var query = window.matchMedia( '( prefers-color-scheme: dark )' ),
				onChange = function () {
					if ( values[ 'andah-theme' ] === 'os' ) {
						applyTheme( 'os' );
					}
				};
			if ( query.addEventListener ) {
				query.addEventListener( 'change', onChange );
			} else if ( query.addListener ) {
				query.addListener( onChange );
			}
		}
	}

	/* --- 4. skip links ------------------------------------------------------
	 * Timeless puts both rails after the article in the DOM and only reorders
	 * them visually with flex. So everything this file lifted into the rails
	 * lands at the very end of the tab order: on [[Dahe]] the contents box is
	 * focusable element 429 of 464, which makes it useless to anyone driving
	 * the page from the keyboard. Two skip links at the top of the header fix
	 * that without touching the DOM order the skin's layout depends on.
	 *
	 * Built last, so it can tell whether there is a contents box to skip to.
	 */

	function buildSkipLinks() {
		var header = document.getElementById( 'mw-header' );
		if ( !header ) {
			return;
		}

		var nav = document.createElement( 'nav' ),
			wanted = [
				[ 'Skip to content', 'mw-content-text' ],
				[ 'Skip to contents', 'andah-toc' ]
			],
			added = 0;

		nav.id = 'andah-skip';
		nav.setAttribute( 'aria-label', 'Skip links' );

		wanted.forEach( function ( pair ) {
			var target = document.getElementById( pair[ 1 ] );
			if ( !target ) {
				return;
			}
			// Lets the target take focus when jumped to, without adding a tab
			// stop of its own on the way past.
			target.setAttribute( 'tabindex', '-1' );
			var link = document.createElement( 'a' );
			link.href = '#' + pair[ 1 ];
			link.textContent = pair[ 0 ];
			nav.appendChild( link );
			added++;
		} );

		if ( added ) {
			header.insertBefore( nav, header.firstChild );
		}
	}

	/* --- start ------------------------------------------------------------- */

	function start() {
		// Build once. Every piece of furniture below is addressed by id, in the
		// CSS and in here, so a second run would produce a second hamburger, a
		// second contents box and a second Appearance panel, and duplicate ids
		// make both copies unaddressable. Cheap insurance against the module
		// being loaded twice.
		if ( document.documentElement.dataset.andahChrome ) {
			return;
		}
		document.documentElement.dataset.andahChrome = '1';

		var values = {};
		PREFS.forEach( function ( pref ) {
			values[ pref.feature ] = readPref( pref );
		} );

		// Text, width and colour go on at once, ahead of the DOM-ready
		// callback. The site module is deferred, so there is a brief moment of
		// the default before these land; doing it here rather than after the
		// panel is built keeps that to one reflow instead of two.
		applyClass( 'andah-text', values[ 'andah-text' ] );
		applyClass( 'andah-width', values[ 'andah-width' ] );
		applyTheme( values[ 'andah-theme' ] );

		$( function () {
			buildNavToggle();
			moveWikiTools();
			buildToc();
			buildAppearance( values );
			// Last: it needs to know whether buildToc produced anything.
			buildSkipLinks();
		} );
	}

	/**
	 * The site module does not depend on mediawiki.storage, so it has to be
	 * asked for; reaching straight for mw.storage would throw and take the
	 * whole file with it.
	 *
	 * Everything below is about one principle: the chrome gets built no matter
	 * what storage does. Three ways it can go wrong, all of them seen:
	 *
	 *   - mw.loader.using may not exist yet. It comes from mediawiki.base, and
	 *     if this file is evaluated first, calling it throws and every piece of
	 *     furniture disappears with no error a reader could act on.
	 *   - the module may reject. Both handlers are start, so that is survivable.
	 *   - the module may simply never settle. A request that hangs leaves a
	 *     promise pending forever, .then never fires, and the page keeps its
	 *     bare Timeless chrome with no clue why. Hence the timeout.
	 *
	 * Losing storage costs the reader their remembered settings for that page
	 * view. Losing the chrome costs them the table of contents, the appearance
	 * controls and the only route to dark mode. The two are not close.
	 */
	function boot() {
		var started = false,
			go = function () {
				if ( started ) {
					return;
				}
				started = true;
				start();
			};

		setTimeout( go, 3000 );

		if ( mw.loader && typeof mw.loader.using === 'function' ) {
			mw.loader.using( [ 'mediawiki.storage' ] ).then( go, go );
		} else {
			go();
		}
	}

	boot();
}() );
